question: Which metal is used for making bulb filaments?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tungsten**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Tungsten (₇₄W) has its atomic number 74.
 
• Tungsten is used in filaments of **incandescent light bulbs.**
 
• Tungsten is used to make **counterfeit gold bars** because of its density which is similar to that of gold.
 
• Tungsten carbide is used in drill bits and mining tools.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Iron (₂₆Fe) has its atomic number 26.

 
 
• Red colour in blood is from the iron in hemoglobin, which helps to carry oxygen from the lungs to cells
 
• Iron used to make electricity pylons, bicycle chains and rifle barrels.
 
 
 
• **Copper** is a chemical element with the symbol Cu and atomic number 29.
 
 
• It is a soft, malleable, and ductile metal with very high thermal and electrical conductivity. 
 
 
 
• **Silicon **is a chemical element with the symbol Si and atomic number 14.
 
 
• It is a hard, brittle crystalline solid with a blue-grey metallic luster, and is a tetravalent metalloid and semiconductor.
